summary: Confirmed heap-buffer-overflow. A reachable type-0x17 option with zero data length passes all candidate guards, requests malloc(3), then performs a four-byte store at offsets 0-3 and a byte store at offset 4. The overflow occurs before the zero-iteration loop, and no upstream minimum-length or allocator-size control blocks the path.

New evidence establishes a normal capacity range of 100000 to 900000 and disproves the iVar4 doubling-overflow hypothesis. It does not prove overall safety: local_774 can persist across multiple 50-step selector segments, so its lifetime accumulation remains potentially unbounded in the available pseudo-C. Feasibility of such a decoded sequence, propagation to the capacity check and writes, universal initializer provenance, and entry-root reachability remain unresolved. Suppression is therefore not justified.
Confirmation requires every proof obligation satisfied

Safety is proven for the out-of-bounds-read class. The history buffer has extent min(dictionary size, output size). The guarded match-copy read rejects wrapped indices outside that extent, while nonnegative indices are below the bounded current position. The apparently unguarded literal-context read can occur only after a successful history operation has established a valid distance; the short-output/full-dictionary split then keeps its adjusted index in bounds. All relevant hypotheses are contradicted, so the candidate is a proven false positive.

The candidate is reachable, but the suspected integer overflow is proven impossible. The resolved callee returns only 0 or 1, so line 114 produces only 1, 2, or 3; line 111 uses only multipliers 0 or 1, and the loop terminates after at most two iterations. All relevant candidate hypotheses are contradicted.

New evidence eliminates one of the entry root's unresolved indirect sites as a route to the candidate: LAB_001133a5 lies inside a small release function with no candidate call. The separate LAB_00112749 site remains unresolved, however, so neither a root-reachable NULL invocation nor complete unreachability is proven. Retain and escalate.
